svg.data-optics-qsfp-dd: 400GE QSFP-DD OpenZR+/ZR/ER4/LR4/SR8/FR4/DR4/DR4+/PLR4; 200GE QSFP56 SR4/FR4; 100GE QSFP28 ZR4/ER4/LR4/SR4 (datasheet compatible transceiver list)
svg.data-zr-capacity: up to 32 QSFP-DD ZR+ modules; the HIG's Figure 12 shades one 32-port band to mark which ports they are - see the zr-port-set gap
svg.data-timing-cable: SMB coaxial with a 10-32UNF-2A connector, for 1PPS and 10MHz
svg.data-console: RJ45 RS-232 plus a micro-USB serial console
svg.data-emc: FCC Part 15, Subpart B, Class A; ICES-003, Class A; EN 55032, Class A; EN 300 386; EN 55035; BSMI (CNS 13438), Class A; VCCI CISPR 32, Class A

rect.data-members: clk-1pps clk-10mhz reset console-usb usb led-sync led-sys led-fan led-ps0 led-ps1 led-id

g.data-description: the 1PPS and 10MHz SMB jacks at the top of the left-hand block, each an input/output on the Premium timing build (datasheet Timing Interfaces)
g.title: clk-1pps

g.data-description: the 1PPS and 10MHz SMB jacks at the top of the left-hand block, each an input/output on the Premium timing build (datasheet Timing Interfaces)
g.title: clk-10mhz

g.data-description: HIG Front Panel LED table, SYNC row - Off (timing/clock synchronization disabled or free-run), Solid Green (timing core synchronized to PTP phase or an external phase source and frequency locked), Blinking Green (synchronized to PTP or an external FREQUENCY source), Solid Amber (acquiring or holdover), Blinking Amber (synchronization failed, or acquiring/holdover timed out)
g.title: led-sync

g.data-description: HIG Front Panel LED table, SYS row - Off (no power), Solid Green (host CPU/BMC boot complete), Solid Amber (power is up but host CPU/BMC boot failed)
g.title: led-sys

g.data-description: HIG Front Panel LED table, FAN row - Off (fans are not initialized), Solid Green (all fans work normal), Blinking Amber (fan fail: one or more fans need service)
g.title: led-fan

g.data-description: HIG Front Panel LED table, PS0 row - Off (no power), Solid Green (PSU0 working normal), Blinking Amber (PSU0 fail, PSU0 needs service)
g.title: led-ps0

g.data-description: HIG Front Panel LED table, PS1 row - Off (no power), Solid Green (PSU1 working normal), Blinking Amber (PSU1 fail, PSU1 needs service)
g.title: led-ps1

g.data-description: HIG Front Panel LED table, ID row - Off (no power), Blinking Blue (beacon feature is enabled on the switch)
g.title: led-id

g.data-description: led-oob-left: HIG Management Port LED table, Left LED - Off (no power), Solid Green (1G link-up), Blinking Green (1G TX/RX activity); the jack's two integrated lamps are led-a/led-b of common/rj45-ganged-eth@1, one placement; before the RJ45 sweep they were two separate placements because std/rj45-ganged@1 contracted none; led-oob-right: HIG Management Port LED table, Right LED - Off (no power), Solid Amber (10M/100M link-up), Blinking Amber (10M/100M TX/RX activity). The two jack lamps do not share a vocabulary, which is why each keeps its own states here rather than a shared default
g.title: oob

g.data-description: the stacked SFP+ pair, '2 x 1/10G SFP+ ports' in the datasheet's physical list. The vendor numbers them 64 and 65 - HIG Figure 10 prints those two numerals in orange, continuing the QSFP-DD run rather than starting a second one - so the rel-pos values are 64 and 65 and index-origin is 0 because the schema allows only 0 or 1 there
g.title: port-64

g.data-description: the stacked SFP+ pair, '2 x 1/10G SFP+ ports' in the datasheet's physical list. The vendor numbers them 64 and 65 - HIG Figure 10 prints those two numerals in orange, continuing the QSFP-DD run rather than starting a second one - so the rel-pos values are 64 and 65 and index-origin is 0 because the schema allows only 0 or 1 there
g.title: port-65

g.data-description: every indicator that belongs to a particular port - the thirty-two QSFP-DD lamp clusters, one above each column of the upper cage band and one below each column of the lower, and the two lamps in the out-of-band jack's own aperture
